Consumed by tools/coverage.py to fill the ledger's target column. == targets IS GENERATED, THE REST IS AUTHORED. Re-run `python3 tools/refresh_migration_targets.py` after any migrator change; `--check` fails when it is stale. It follows the call graph from each class's entry point in +migrators_j (falling back to +migrators, which is where V_eta lands when +migrators_j has no file) through private/ helpers and local subfunctions, resolving class names passed as parameters at their call sites, and reuses tools/status_board.py's statement-level extractor so a `superclasses` entry is never read as a document class. It rewrites a row only when every reachable emission resolved; where one did not (element, measurement, ontology_table_row, subjectmeasurement -- all pick their leaf class at runtime) the row can only GAIN, never lose. A migrator that mints nothing keeps a target naming ITSELF and loses any target naming another class. == ON session_relative_reference, WHICH IS A CONTRADICTION BETWEEN TWO COMMITTED RECORDS AND IS NOT RESOLVED HERE. 36 rows name `session_relative_reference`, because private/jSessionAnchor.m:19 mints it and every observation migrator calls that helper. The signed time model (V_eta_time_reference_model_plan.md) COLLAPSES it, with seven siblings, into `relative_time_reference`. Both are true of different moments, and both halves are already in the code: private/jEpochClockReferences.m:141 and private/jClockAlignmentBodies.m:174 mint `relative_time_reference` today, which is why 4 rows name the new class while 36 name the old one. So a `session_relative_reference` target is a statement about what pass 1 EMITS TODAY, never a decision that the class survives; the decision is the sign-off in the plan document, and tools/status_board.py's RETIRED_BY_ITS_OWN_DECISION carries the same reading. Rewriting the 36 rows to a class their migrators do not emit would make this file describe an intention rather than the code.
